A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReinFlow, with matching algorithms, theoretical results, and benchmark experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated locomotion and manipulation experiments, timing measurements, and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments and adds ablation results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same Gaussian noise injection, joint trajectory likelihood, PPO optimization, and jointly trained velocity and noise networks. Action chunking, optional regularization, and discarding the noise network after fine-tuning are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gym locomotion tasks, three Franka Kitchen demonstration variants, and Robomimic Can, Square, and Transport tasks. The additional ablations vary algorithm settings within existing tasks.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Figures 1–3 and 11–12 are retained, including DPPO, FQL, and Gaussian policies where applicable. Figure 3 adds panel legends without introducing new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Table 9b changes Transport’s reported actor learning rate from cos(3.5e-5, 3.5e-5) to cos(3.5e-6, 3.5e-6), without establishing that the benchmark was rerun. Appendix F introduces additional controlled entropy, noise-conditioning, and noise-scale settings; the main evaluation protocols otherwise remain stable.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds entropy regularization and noise-scale ablations in Kitchen-complete, plus state-only versus state-and-time noise conditioning in Humanoid. These extend existing design-choice analyses to additional retained environments rather than introducing a substantially different analysis program.

E5.justification: v6 removes the basic seed identifiers 0, 42, and 3407 from Appendix E, Tables 3 and 5, and the Figure 13 caption, replacing them with generic descriptions. The three/five-run counts and mean ± standard deviation convention remain; the two additional Kitchen seed identifiers remain in Appendix G.2.

E6.justification: Appendix F adds results such as 99.00 ± 0.75% Kitchen-complete success with entropy coefficient 0.1, alongside the retained unregularized 96.17 ± 3.65%. It also reports new noise-conditioning and noise-scale outcomes. Figure 3(a) omits the final plotted checkpoint, while the main numerical results in Tables 3–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the discounted-return sum’s starting index from h=1 to h=0, aligning it with Appendix A. Theorem 4.1, its assumptions and proof, and the action-chunking derivation otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v6 narrows the introductory contribution list by removing the explicit contribution of establishing a general policy-gradient theory, although Theorem 4.1 remains. The central online flow-policy fine-tuning claim and headline performance and efficiency claims are retained.

C2.justification: Appendix F explicitly distinguishes noise injection’s likelihood-computation role from optional entropy-based exploration control and interprets the added ablations as supporting generalization across reward structures. Section 7 adds clearer limitations concerning noise tuning and untested scaling to large vision-language-action models.

D1.justification: Besides the revised Transport learning rate, v6 explicitly advertises code, models, and checkpoints through the existing project website. Its checklist still describes release as forthcoming, leaving availability internally inconsistent. Most architecture, hardware, and implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds Sauer’s Numerical Analysis reference and removes the Csiszar–Shields information-theory tutorial and DeepSeekMath references. Positioning relative to DPPO, FQL, Flow-GRPO, and ORW-CFM-W2 remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Many main-text paragraphs are rewritten or condensed, particularly Related Work and the likelihood and noise-network explanations. v6 removes the notation paragraph, expands the conclusion, inserts a checklist and Discussion appendix, and moves the reproduction appendix from F to G. The editorial revision extends well beyond local copyediting.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS format changes typography, text width, author layout, and the sizing and placement of displays throughout. Figure 2 loses its Kitchen wall-time panel, Figure 3 gains panel legends, Figure 5b changes colors and line styling, and Appendix F adds two ablation tables.

improvement.justification: The added Appendix F ablations strengthen support for the noise and regularization design choices, while the expanded limitations make applicability boundaries clearer. These are useful but limited gains because the method and main benchmark evidence remain largely unchanged. Reduced seed transparency and contradictory resource-release wording temper the improvement.
